question: An AI cannot do the hashing (proved: EXP-SHA-LADDER, full-round accuracy 50.4% vs 50% chance). Its only route to value in mining is deciding WHEN to hash. So: across the electricity-price / hardware-efficiency plane, where does the difficulty forecast actually change a run-or-curtail decision, and what is that worth?
why_this_was_needed: FINDINGS records binary run/stop decision value as ~$0, but that was one scenario (E=$0.06/kWh) where the miner is profitable whatever difficulty does, so the decision never flips. A single scenario cannot support a general claim. This maps 32 scenarios spanning $0.03-$0.25/kWh and 17-30 J/TH.

scenario.economics: parametric; only the difficulty forecasts are empirical (champion vs naive, P1 test epochs)

headline.read: On a 1 PH/s farm turning over $1,620 per epoch, the best the difficulty forecast can do for the run/curtail decision is $2.10 - and a PERFECT difficulty oracle caps at the same $2.10. In five of 32 scenarios the forecast makes the decision WORSE than ignoring it.

why_it_is_worth_nothing: The run/stop decision only flips when profit is within one difficulty move of zero. A difficulty move is ~3.3% of revenue. So the decision is live only in a thin band around breakeven - and inside that band profit is by definition ~$0, so calling it correctly earns ~$0. The forecast is accurate but the decision it feeds is worthless.

what_actually_drives_the_decision.electricity_price: at $0.03/kWh a 25 J/TH miner runs 109 of 109 epochs; at $0.25/kWh it runs 33. THAT is the decision.
what_actually_drives_the_decision.conclusion: The run/curtail decision is dominated by electricity price and BTC price. Difficulty is a rounding error in it.

verdict: DECISION BAND FOUND BUT ECONOMICALLY EMPTY - generalizes the single-scenario $0 result to the whole realistic parameter space
strategic_consequence: An AI meant to decide WHEN to mine should forecast ELECTRICITY PRICE, not difficulty. Difficulty forecasting remains defensible for forward-selling/hashprice exposure (a linear exposure, where the 3.3% does translate into dollars) but not for the on/off decision. This is the third independent line of evidence that the difficulty track is the smallest component: EXP25 put it at 8-26% of revenue variance, the VOI map at $32k of $139k perfect-information value, and now the curtail decision at ~$0.
